newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFO begins probe into former Wickes bosses.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFO begins probe into former Wickes bosses.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Wednesday it was probing the former senior management of Wickes, the British Do-It-Yourself retailer which this summer was shaken by accounting irregularities.

"The SFO has launched an investigation into the former senior management of Wickes," an SFO spokesman told Reuters. The probe is being carried out jointly with the Metropolitan Police and the present management of the company is co-operating fully with the SFO's enquiries.
UK's SFO begins probe into former Wickes bosses

"No one has been arrested or charged and we have not executed any search warrants," James O'Donoghue said, adding that the SFO had taken on the case on November 20 but had not announced its involvement "for operational reasons".

O'Donoghue said he could not name any of the former senior managers under investigation. He said the probe followed on from reports produced by accountants Price Waterhouse and law firm Linklaters & Paine for the company.
"These investigations have led to the SFO having the reasonable grounds it requires to be able to launch a criminal investigation," he said.

Misleading accounting at Wickes was uncovered in June. This had led to the overstatement of group profit by tens of millions of pounds over the last five years. The news rocked the Wickes share price, leading to its suspension and a boardroom purge.
